incident-bot: PAGE: oncall-sre - high /customer 429 rate from tenant 'Peregrine Labs' in us-west-2 VPC. Error spike started ~T0+3m, automated alerting shows >15% 429s over 1m :rotating_light:

sara (oncall): Ack. Joining. Which pool is this hitting? dedicated or shared?

alex (sre): It’s hitting the peregrine-dedicated-pool-2 (dedicated) — consistent 429s from their tenant id. I see their prefix cache utilization is normal, not KV cache related.

incident-bot: ALERT DETAILS: 429s (rate limit) from tenant=tenant_peregrine, model=t5-large-quant, region=us-west-2, p50 latency ~85ms, call volume ~380 rps (baseline 70 rps).

jamal (acct mgmt): FYI Peregrine is on an enterprise VPC contract with burst allowances but no open emergency override in UI. They have an ongoing migration but need immediate relief; I can authorize a temporary burst for up to 3x for 30m if engineering confirms safe.

sara (oncall): Good to know. We should apply a targeted per-tenant burst override rather than global pool bump. Can someone run the emergency override runbook? Link: https://console.redwood.internal/runbooks/tenant-override

alex (sre): On it. Running admin patch now. Command:```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://admin.internal/api/v1/tenants/tenant_peregrine/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"rate_multiplier":3, "duration_minutes":30, "reason":"Emergency burst for customer impact"}'
```

ops-bot: change_request created CR-9872 by alex. Audit link: https://audit.internal/cr/9872

alex (sre): Applied override, response 200. New per-tenant limit multiplier=3 for 30m. Pushing a canary adjust to one node in the pool then global.

sara (oncall): Observing metrics… 1m update: 429 rate dropped from 18% -> 3%. Traffic normalized. Can we keep an eye for error oscillations?

maya (eng-ml): Noted. Model variant t5-large-quant has high memory pressure under this pattern; if we see mem OOMs switch policy to reroute heavy requests to t5-medium-quant as fallback. But prefer keeping same model for quality.

kevin (support): I’ve notified Peregrine via #customer-peregrine (private) that we’re applying a temporary burst. Jamal is on the call to approve any further extension.

jamal (acct mgmt): Confirmed. Approving 3x for 30m. If they still need more after that we’ll take it to finance for an addendum.

peter (infra): Quick note — pool headroom is limited. If Peregrine sustains after 30m we’ll need to either: a) spin up a reserved node in us-west-2 (tied to dedicated pool), or b) start diverting low-priority requests to the shared fallback cluster. Which do we prefer?

sara (oncall): We'll monitor. If after 20m their QPS > 250 sustained, move to diversion plan (b) to avoid affecting other dedicated tenants. Alex, please prepare the diversion script and test on canary.

alex (sre): Will prepare. Draft diversion command (canary):```bash
# divert traffic for tenant_peregrine to shared-fallback-route
curl -X POST "https://router.internal/api/v1/divert" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"tenant_peregrine","target":"shared-fallback","percent":20}'
```

ops-bot: CR-9872 updated: status=mitigated, mitigation=tenant override 3x, ttl=30m.

incident-bot: NOTE: page resolved? No. Currently mitigated. Next step: keep watch for 30m and schedule postmortem with SRE + CS + Sales.

sara (oncall): Thanks all. Postmortem owners: alex (SRE), jamal (Account), maya (Model lead). Action items: create short timeline, check quota policy gap that prevented self-serve override, recommend product change to allow scheduled emergency bursts for enterprise VPCs.

kevin (support): I’ll log the customer incident and include the current metrics snapshot. Kept them in the loop: they’re expecting a follow-up after the 30m window.

jamal (acct mgmt): I'll draft the customer-facing note and confirm whether they want us to apply an extended temporary commit.

sara (oncall): Closing command — patch to revoke override at T0+30m will be scheduled automatically. If anyone sees re-escalation react here or call the oncall pager. Good work. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: SUMMARY: mitigation applied (tenant override x3 for 30m). 429s reduced to acceptable levels. Owners assigned. CR-9872 linked.
